history: Cleveland's Burke Lakefront Airport became a temporary street circuit in the early 1980s, hosting CART IndyCar races. The full circuit layout, the longer of the two configurations, was the primary track used for these events. The inaugural race in 1982 saw a thrilling victory for Mario Andretti. The circuit quickly became a popular stop on the CART calendar, known for its challenging layout and the unique backdrop of Lake Erie and the Cleveland skyline. Races continued throughout the 80s and 90s, with the last IndyCar race held on the full circuit in 2007. While other forms of racing have occasionally visited the airport, the IndyCar era remains the track's most prominent period.
atmosphere: The roar of IndyCars bouncing off the concrete barriers and temporary grandstands, mixed with the distinctive smell of racing fuel and the ever-present breeze off Lake Erie – that's Cleveland. The lakefront setting offered stunning views, and the temporary nature of the track gave it a raw, almost rebellious energy. The crowds were always enthusiastic, drawn by the speed and danger of racing so close to the city center. You could feel the vibrations of the cars through your feet as they thundered past, a visceral experience that made Cleveland a memorable stop on the racing calendar.
trackCharacter: The full circuit at Burke Lakefront Airport was a true test of nerve and precision. Its long straights were punctuated by a series of challenging corners, demanding both straight-line speed and precise braking. The bumpy surface added another layer of complexity, requiring drivers to constantly adjust their lines and manage their car's balance. The configuration rewarded aggressive driving, but also punished mistakes severely, making it a thrilling and unpredictable challenge.

famousCorners.name: Turn 1
famousCorners.description: A fast, sweeping right-hander that immediately tests the driver's commitment and car setup.
famousCorners.challenge: Carrying enough speed through the corner to maintain momentum down the following straight.

famousCorners.name: Turn 3
famousCorners.description: A tight hairpin, one of the slowest corners on the track, providing a key overtaking opportunity.
famousCorners.challenge: Braking late and accurately to avoid locking up the tires and losing time.

famousCorners.name: Turn 5
famousCorners.description: A quick left-hander that requires precision and a good car balance.
famousCorners.challenge: Maintaining the optimal line and avoiding understeer to maximize exit speed.

famousCorners.name: Turn 8
famousCorners.description: A long, gradual right-hand bend that tests the car's lateral grip.
famousCorners.challenge: Finding the right balance between speed and grip to maintain momentum through the corner.

famousCorners.name: Turn 10
famousCorners.description: The final corner, a quick right-hander that leads onto the main straight.
famousCorners.challenge: Getting a clean exit to maximize speed down the straight and set up an overtaking opportunity.

weatherNotes: Being located on the shores of Lake Erie, Cleveland's weather can be unpredictable. Lake-effect rain and fog are common, especially in the spring and fall. Wind can also be a significant factor, affecting car handling and aerodynamics, especially on the long straights. Sudden changes in temperature can also impact tire performance.
drivingAdvice: The key to a fast lap on the full Cleveland circuit is maintaining momentum. The bumpy surface makes it difficult to carry speed through the corners, so it's crucial to find the right balance between aggression and smoothness. Be patient with the throttle, especially on corner exits, to avoid wheelspin. Qualifying is critical, as overtaking can be challenging on the narrow track. Don't be afraid to use the full width of the track, but be aware of the concrete barriers – there's very little margin for error.
famousRaces: 1982: Mario Andretti's victory in the inaugural race, marking a strong start for the Cleveland event.
1992: Al Unser Jr. wins a thrilling race, battling through the field after a difficult qualifying session.
1995: Bobby Rahal's emotional victory in his final full season of racing, a highlight of his career.
localCulture: Cleveland is a city with a rich industrial history and a vibrant arts and culture scene. The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame is a must-see for music fans. The city's culinary scene is diverse, with a focus on hearty, Midwestern fare. Paddock life at Cleveland was always lively, with teams and fans mingling in the city's bars and restaurants after the races. The local community embraced the race, creating a festive atmosphere throughout the weekend.
